newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sub-continent gold demand seen good for prices.
newsitem.headline: Indian sub-continent gold demand seen good for prices.

text.p: Fresh wedding season demand for gold in India and jewellery buying for the Ramadan holiday in Pakistan would keep gold prices firm on the Indian sub-continent in the near term, dealers and analysts said on Monday.

Dealers in Bombay said harvesting of early summer crops also coincided with the second phase of India's wedding season, beginning in mid-January after a month's break. Indians traditionally get married in the winter months.
"There'll be enough seasonal demand to push up prices," said Makhan Lal Damani, president of the Bombay Bullion Association.
India's summer harvest and wedding season lasts until May.
In the week to Monday gold prices on the Bombay bullion market lost 40 rupees per 10 grams to 4,880 rupees after recovering 80 rupees in the previous two trading sessions.
"The recovery followed a similar trend in the world market which triggered speculative buying locally," said Damani.

In Hong Kong gold was traded at $358.40/90 an ounce at midday on Monday against New York's close of $358.80/$359.30. During the previous week it fell to fresh three-year lows below $355 an ounce before shortcovering and Japanese buying helped it recover slightly.

"Lower domestic prices in India have reduced the profit margins on imports, acting as a disincentive to bring in gold," Damani said. "I expect prices to rise due to the low availability of gold this week."
In Karachi, Pakistan's main commercial city, gold prices rose 28 rupees per 10 grams to 5,138 rupees in the week to Sunday.

Dealers said they expected the precious metal to post further gains on good demand for jewellery during the Islamic fasting month of Ramadan. Moslems in most countries observed the start of Ramadan on Friday.
Karachi dealers said the wedding season in February could also push up demand for gold during that month.
In Dubai, the hub of gold trade in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), prices have fallen in line with the weak global market despite improved demand on the first few days of Ramadan.
"Demand is good at the moment. It is better than it has been in the past few weeks," a gold wholesaler said on Sunday.

They said the market was coming out of a slow year-end period, with sharply lower international prices, the Indian wedding season and more liberal rules on gold imports into India -- the world's biggest gold market -- bolstering the sales outlook.
"Normally, demand is good in the first few days of Ramadan, but slows towards the end of the month when people are preparing for Eid," a trader said.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMS IN U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $1=35.85 Indian rupees, 40.22 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams)
* Bombay prices January 13 & 6, Karachi and Dubai January 12 & 5.
